newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian summer crops head for record - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian summer crops head for record - ABARE.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) has held its forecast of Australia's summer crop production in 1996/97 at a record 3.85 million tonnes.
The forecast is steady with ABARE's Australian Crop Report forecast issued last month.

Total plantings to winter crops are forecast to decline by 2.5 percent in 1997/98 in expectation of lower prices, ABARE said in its overview on grains in its Australian Commodities March quarter publication.

Forecast relative returns for winter crops, combined with an expected return to more usual crop rotations, favour increased plantings in 1997/98 of oilseeds and pulses, particularly canola, at the expense of wheat and barley, it said.
Canola production is forecast to jump to 822,000 tonnes in 1997/98 from an estimated 616,000 tonnes in 1996/97. Production in 1995/96 was 561,000 tonnes.
Canola exports for 1997/98 are forecast to rise to 569,000 tonnes from 414,000 tonnes but prices are forecast to slip to A$325 a tonne in 1997/98 from A$340 a tonne in 1996/97.
